question: Who founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotirao Phule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jyotirao Phule founded the **Satya Shodhak Samaj** in 1873 in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• The primary aim of the organization was to achieve **social equality** and eradicate caste discrimination and untouchability.
 
• Satya Shodhak Samaj focused on spreading education and promoting rational thinking, especially among **lower-caste communities.**
 
• Phule was a pioneer of social reform and worked to uplift marginalized sections, including women and Dalits, through his initiatives.
 
• The organization emphasized the values of justice, equality, and universal human rights, rejecting religious orthodoxy and caste hierarchies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotirao Phule**

 
 
• He is widely regarded as one of the first prominent social reformers in India who fought against casteism and patriarchy.
 
• Phule and his wife, Savitribai Phule, are known for their contributions to women’s education and empowerment in India.
 
• He authored several works, including the seminal book **"Gulamgiri"** (Slavery), which criticized caste oppression.
 
• Jyotirao Phule was also the first person to use the term **"Dalit"** to describe marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Satya Shodhak Samaj's Objectives**
 
 
• The organization aimed to create a society based on principles of **equality, liberty, and fraternity.**
 
• It rejected Brahmanical dominance, advocating for self-respect and dignity for all castes.
 
• It encouraged members to perform marriages without priests and rituals, emphasizing rationalism and simplicity.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Satya Shodhak Samaj**
 
 
• The movement played a significant role in awakening the oppressed communities in Maharashtra and India at large.
 
• It laid the groundwork for later social reform movements, including those led by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• It inspired similar efforts to combat caste-based discrimination in other parts of India.
